issues.title: Unused variable causes compilation warning
issues.description: The code declares an unused variable 'unused_flag' that triggers a compilation warning, causing the build to fail when -Werror flag is enabled
issues.rule_name: Build Must Compile Without Warnings When -Werror is Enabled

issues.title: Buffer overflow in HPEXPIREAT propagation array
issues.description: The argv array is declared with size 5 (robj *argv[5]) which allocates indices 0-4, but the code attempts to access argv[5] which is out of bounds. This array is used to propagate the HPEXPIREAT command to replicas and AOF when a field has expiration. The buffer overflow can cause memory corruption, crash the server, or lead to undefined behavior during replication.

issues.title: Off-by-one error in field expiration comparison
issues.description: The expiration check uses strict greater-than (>) instead of greater-than-or-equal (>=) when comparing expiredAt with commandTimeSnapshot(). This causes fields that expire at exactly the current timestamp to be incorrectly treated as expired. In high-frequency operations, this can lead to premature field expiration and data loss, especially affecting the HINCRBYFLOAT operation's ability to preserve field TTL correctly.

issues.title: Memory leak in HPEXPIREAT propagation
issues.description: The code creates a new string object via createStringObjectFromLongLong(expireat) and stores it in argv[2], but fails to call decrRefCount(argv[2]) after propagating the command. This causes a memory leak every time HINCRBYFLOAT is executed on a field with an expiration time. Over time, repeated calls will accumulate leaked string objects, gradually consuming server memory and potentially leading to out-of-memory conditions.

issues.title: Out-of-bounds write to argv array may trigger -Warray-bounds (and is UB)
issues.description: The code declares `robj *argv[5];` (valid indices 0..4) but then writes `argv[5]` and passes an argument count of 6 to `alsoPropagate`. This is undefined behavior and can also trigger compiler diagnostics such as `-Warray-bounds`, which will fail the build under `-Werror`.
issues.rule_name: Build Must Compile Without Warnings When -Werror is Enabled

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14227 - Fix HINCRBYFLOAT removes field expiration on replica

structured_output.summary:
The PR fixes a master/replica divergence: HINCRBYFLOAT was rewritten to HSET, and on replicas HSET clears a field's TTL, while the master keeps it. The fix makes `hashTypeGetValue` optionally return the field's expire time through a new `expiredAt` out-parameter. When `HINCRBYFLOAT` hits a field that has a TTL, it now propagates `HSET` followed by `HPEXPIREAT ... FIELDS 1 <field>` as a MULTI/EXEC via `alsoPropagate`. Fields without a TTL still propagate as a plain HSET. The test added to `hash-field-expire.tcl` checks both the replication stream shape and the end-to-end replica state.

The approach is sound and the test is well targeted. However, the propagation code has a real memory-safety bug: `robj *argv[5]` is written at index 5 and then passed with length 6, which is a stack out-of-bounds write on every HINCRBYFLOAT against a field with a TTL. There is also a leaked refcount on the expire-time string object. These need fixing before merge."
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `argv[5]` write into a 5-element stack array (and the matching `alsoPropagate(..., 6, ...)`) is undefined behaviour that can corrupt the stack on a common code path, so it is a blocker. The leaked `createStringObjectFromLongLong` reference is a smaller but real per-call leak. The remaining items are cleanups and notes. The design and the test coverage are otherwise good.

architecture.overview:
Redis hash commands run in `src/t_hash.c`. Writes are replicated and appended to AOF by rewriting the client's argv, which the command handler does after it has applied the change. Before this PR, `hincrbyfloatCommand` rewrote itself into `HSET key field <final value>` so that float formatting differences cannot diverge between master, replicas and AOF replay. `HSET` on a replica clears any existing field TTL, but the master keeps it, so the two drift apart. Field reads go through `hashTypeGetValue`, which handles listpack, listpackex and hashtable encodings and applies lazy expiry.

The PR adds an optional `uint64_t *expiredAt` out-parameter to `hashTypeGetValue`, so `hincrbyfloatCommand` can learn whether the field has a TTL. When it does, the command stops its own propagation with `preventCommandPropagation` and calls `alsoPropagate` twice, first with the rewritten HSET and then with a synthetic HPEXPIREAT carrying the original absolute expire time. Redis wraps the two entries in MULTI/EXEC, so the replica applies both. A new shared object `shared.fields` supplies the FIELDS token. The existing `hexpire`/`hpexpireat` replication machinery is what the replica already understands.
steps: Entry point: a client sends `HINCRBYFLOAT key field incr`, which dispatches to `hincrbyfloatCommand` in `src/t_hash.c`. The command reads the current value through `hashTypeGetValue` with `HFE_LAZY_EXPIRE`.

The PR extends `hashTypeGetValue` with a nullable `expiredAt` out-parameter. Its callers that don't need the TTL pass NULL, and it uses a local dummy in that case. The lookup helpers `hashTypeGetFromListpack` and `hashTypeGetFromHashTable` now write the TTL through this pointer.

In `hincrbyfloatCommand`, a field with a TTL sets `has_expiration`. After the value is written, the command rewrites argv to HSET as before. It then calls `preventCommandPropagation` and uses `alsoPropagate` to emit HSET, then HPEXPIREAT. Those two entries are wrapped in MULTI/EXEC on the replication stream and in the AOF.
Fields without a TTL still take the original path, so the replication stream stays as a single HSET. This keeps the common case unchanged.
The new Tcl test asserts the exact replication stream shape for TTL and non-TTL fields, then starts a replica and checks that the TTL and value match the master after `HINCRBYFLOAT`.

diagrams.title: HINCRBYFLOAT propagation after this PR
diagrams.description: Shows how hincrbyfloatCommand decides between one HSET and a MULTI of HSET plus HPEXPIREAT, and where each path ends up.

flowchart TD

diagrams.title: Master-replica propagation of a TTL field
diagrams.description: Shows that the replica receives HSET and HPEXPIREAT as a transaction, so the field keeps its TTL after the update.
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant M as Master
    participant R as Replica
    C->>M: HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1
    M->>M: hashTypeGetValue reads f1 and its TTL
    M->>M: apply new value via hashTypeSet with KEEP_TTL
    M->>R: MULTI
    M->>R: HSET h1 f1 <value>
    M->>R: HPEXPIREAT h1 <ms> FIELDS 1 f1
    M->>R: EXEC
    R->>R: HSET keeps TTL, then HPEXPIREAT restores it

findings.title: Out-of-bounds write: argv[5] on a 5-element array
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, inside `hincrbyfloatCommand` (around lines 2306-2313), the local array `robj *argv[5]` is indexed up to `argv[5]` and then passed to `alsoPropagate` with length 6. That is a stack out-of-bounds write. Change the array to hold six elements so it matches the HPEXPIREAT argument count (`HPEXPIREAT key time FIELDS 1 field`), and keep the length passed to `alsoPropagate` consistent with it. Don't change the argument values. Follow the same `alsoPropagate` usage as the HSET call just above.

findings.title: Refcount leak on the expire-time string object
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` creates `argv[2]` with `createStringObjectFromLongLong(expireat)` for the synthetic HPEXPIREAT. That object is never released. After the `alsoPropagate(c->db->id, argv, 6, ...)` call, add `decrRefCount(argv[2]);` so the reference we own is dropped. Check in `src/server.c` that `alsoPropagate` retains its own reference. Keep the rest of the propagation logic unchanged.

findings.title: Unused variable and redundant flag in hincrbyfloatCommand
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` declares `int unused_flag` (around line 2243), which is never used, and `int has_expiration` (around line 2242), which only mirrors `expireat != EB_EXPIRE_TIME_INVALID`. Remove `unused_flag`. Replace `has_expiration` with a direct check on `expireat` in the `if (has_expiration)` block near line 2297, and drop the assignment in the GETF_OK branch near line 2263.

findings.title: Silent change in expiry boundary from >= to >
findings.body:
`hashTypeGetValue` used to treat a field as live when `expiredAt >= now`. It now requires `expiredAt > now`, so a field whose TTL is exactly the current millisecond is treated as expired. The change is probably correct, and it matches how the rest of HFE treats `expire <= now` as expired. But it changes read behaviour at a one-millisecond boundary, and the PR description doesn't mention it. It should be called out in the commit message or a comment so reviewers and maintainers know it is intentional.

::diff{file="src/t_hash.c" lines="742-742"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hashTypeGetValue` (around line 742) changed the live-field check from `*expiredAt >= commandTimeSnapshot()` to `*expiredAt > commandTimeSnapshot()`. Confirm this matches the expiry convention used by the other HFE paths, and add a brief comment or commit-message note that the boundary is intentionally exclusive so a field expiring at exactly now counts as expired. Don't change the comparison unless the convention check shows it is inconsistent.

findings.title: Test covers the replication stream and replica state for TTL fields
findings.body:
The new test checks two things. First, it asserts the exact replication stream: HSET for a field without a TTL, and MULTI with HSET then HPEXPIREAT for a field with one. Second, it starts a real replica and checks that the TTL and value match the master after the increment. It covers both the TTL-preserving path and the plain-HSET path in one test, which is the regression that matters here.

::diff{file="tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl" lines="1269-1320"}

findings.title: Missing AOF restart coverage and a test for the out-of-bounds path
findings.body:
The PR description says the change must also keep AOF replay consistent, but the test only checks the replication stream and a live replica. Nothing restarts the server from AOF to confirm that the MULTI with HSET and HPEXPIREAT replays to the same TTL. The out-of-bounds write above would not be caught by this test either, since it only exercises the value and TTL. An AOF reload test with `debug loadaof` on a TTL field would close that gap.

::diff{file="tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl" lines="1269-1276"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl`, the new HINCRBYFLOAT test (around lines 1269-1320) covers the replication stream and a live replica, but not AOF replay. Add a step that sets a TTL field, runs HINCRBYFLOAT on it, then runs `r debug loadaof` and checks that the value and TTL are preserved. Follow the surrounding tests for AOF setup and assertion style. Keep the existing replication assertions.

findings.title: Shared object and signature change are clean and NULL-tolerant
findings.body:
The `expiredAt` parameter is optional. Passing NULL points it at a local dummy, so the existing callers (`hashTypeGetValueObject`, `hashTypeExists`, `hincrbyCommand`, `addHashFieldToReply`, `hstrlenCommand`) only needed a trailing `NULL` added. The new `shared.fields` object follows the existing pattern in `createSharedObjects` and is declared in the same struct list. Both changes are small and easy to review.

::diff{file="src/t_hash.c" lines="716-726"}
